## Pain

Windows `ts:check-lane` / release Step 5 still dies at 20 minutes (exit 124) on `vitest --coverage`. Cheapening git-worktree fixtures (#4567) does not close that wall clock. Isolated evidence on the originating issue: expensive files are mostly CLI boots, not only `dispatcher-effective-root` / `dispatcher-spawn-dest`. There is no measured full-suite Windows coverage baseline before/after.

## What this is not

- Not #4567 (stop per-it `git worktree add`, inject the existing git-runner seam, retain the suite tee on exit 124, correct the vitest.config spawn-economics comment).
- Not raising the 20-minute hang-detector timeout except as last possibility after a measured remaining gap. Stretching that timeout to fit a slow suite is a #3156 miss. `--skip-ci` is not the product close.
- Not 8-worker git-worktree lock contention. Round 1 on #4567 refuted that premise: each case builds its own temp repo.

#4567 pain-audit 5686594993: two-file cheapening does not shed the measured gap. Recut/Handoff 5686686843 / 5686687909 named ranked expensive files plus a measured Windows coverage baseline as leftover. Operator lock 5685476402: timeout last.

## Finding 2 — `sharpens-framing`

**"Still dies after cheapening" is the pre-ship remainder, not a post-ship full-suite number. The 124 is armed on release Step 5, not on the `ts:check-lane` verb.**

Evidence. Batches 1-4 wall clocks are 231.05 + 123.14 + 106.85 + 115.29 = 576.33s for 400 files. This SHA has 1219 `*.test.ts` files under the vitest include. Straight-line floor is about 29 minutes. The originating audit already showed the named pair could not close a ~9-minute gap. I found no post-cheapening full-suite tee or exit-124 log on this host. `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:packages/core/src/release/constants.ts` keeps `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 * 60 * 1000`. `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:packages/core/src/release/preflight.ts` is the path that arms it (`runReleaseCheck` -> `timeoutMs: RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`, exit 124). `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:packages/cli/src/check.ts` calls `dispatchTaskCheck` with no timeout. `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts` uses `spawnSync` with no timeout. `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml` has `timeout-minutes: 20` on `pnpm run test`; `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:.github/workflows/ci.yml` points that lane at `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. Failure mode. A builder treats the pre-cheapening file ranks as post-cheapening ranks, or chases the `ts:check-lane` verb as if it emitted 124.

Disposition consequence. State P1 as the supervised Windows coverage kill (release Step 5 / suite supervisor). Keep a measured post-#4567 Windows `--coverage` wall clock as acceptance. Do not equate the Ubuntu CI step timeout with that kill.

## Finding 3 — `sharpens-framing`

**Existing mechanisms already name the cheapenings. A new hang-detector timeout or a new runner is not the first inventory.**

Evidence, all `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:<path>`:

- `vitest.config.ts` already records Windows spawn throughput as concurrency-independent, forbids lowering `maxWorkers` or re-serializing files, and names partitioning spawn-heavy suites into their own vitest project as the next step. `packages/core/src/vitest-runner/vitest-config-contract.test.ts` locks those forbids (`fileParallelism: false` refused; `maxWorkers: winMaxWorkers` required).
- `packages/cli/src/gates-cli/_helpers.ts` `runDeftTs` is `spawnSync(process.execPath, [binPath(), verb, ...])`. Coverage `exclude` in `vitest.config.ts` includes `packages/cli/src/bin.ts`. Those boots do not credit coverage of the child process.
- In-process siblings already sit next to the spawn layer: `run` from `packages/cli/src/policy.ts` and `packages/cli/src/hook-dispatch.ts`; `runSessionStart` in `session-ritual-cli.test.ts`.
- The #4567 share-plus-afterEach lease reset is already in the two dispatcher files. `hook-dispatch-worktree.test.ts` still uses the old per-`it` `fixture()`.
- Last-file progress already shipped (`packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/progress.ts`).
- Hang-detector raise stays last (operator lock 5685476402). `--skip-ci` is already a flagged skip, not a product close. Stretching the 20-minute supervisor so a slow suite fits is a #3156 miss (`content/docs/gate-integrity.md`).
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` Slow tests (#975): a test over ~1s should be refactored onto injected seams, not hidden.

Failure mode. The next ship edits `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`, or invents a parallel CLI harness, or sets `fileParallelism: false` and collides with the contract test, while those seams sit unused.

Disposition consequence. Rank remaining files, then reuse: share-plus-reset for leftover git-worktree clones; in-process `run` / injected git for CLI parity; the already-named vitest project split for spawn-heavy leftovers that must stay out of process. Timeout last.

## Finding 4 — `sharpens-framing`

**Occupancy-lease tests, leftover git-worktree fixtures, and CLI process boots are three classes. Sharing occupancy fixtures is the risky one.**

Injection / swarm lens (worktrees, concurrency, shared state). `dispatcher.test.ts` and `dispatcher-grok-identity.test.ts` write occupancy leases on per-`it` temp roots. That independence is what the occupancy cases exist to protect. Sharing those roots without a proven reset reintroduces order-dependence on `occupancy.json` / child-occupancy. `runDeftTs` is a different spawn class (Windows execute-scan chokepoint, already documented in `vitest.config.ts`). `hook-dispatch-worktree.test.ts` is the git-worktree class again and can reuse the #4567 share-plus-reset.

Failure mode. A "share fixtures" pass aimed at wall clock collapses occupancy isolation, or a "CLI boots" pass leaves the occupancy cluster (267.4s + 114.7s in the same batch-5d log) untouched.

Disposition consequence. Record the three classes on the bound P1. Git-worktree leftover may reuse the existing share-plus-reset. Occupancy stays per-`it` unless a reset is shown to keep cases independent. CLI boots go in-process or out of the coverage lane.

## Footnotes

`footnote` — GHA TypeScript coverage at this SHA is Ubuntu. There is no Windows workflow `runs-on` in `.github/workflows`. CI can stay green while Windows release Step 5 exits 124.

`footnote` — `CI_VITEST_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` in `packages/core/src/release/constants.ts` has no consumer. The live CI cap is workflow `timeout-minutes: 20`.

`footnote` — `vitest-batch-2.log` (not in the origin top-9 table) adds more CLI-spawn files at 111-117s each (`verify-completed-tracked`, `verify-branch`, `verify-story-ready`). "Mostly CLI boots" is directionally larger than the top-9, and still does not license dropping occupancy and leftover git-worktree.

## Road not taken

I considered classifying Finding 1 as `sharpens-framing` because the body hedges with "mostly CLI boots". I rejected that. The title and Stop 1 gate stamp assert an exclusive cause, and that is what a later harvest will scope.

Steelman: after the #4567 pair is shared, remaining cost is majority CLI, and "not git-worktree" means "not that pair". What would flip Finding 1 to non-blocking: a post-ship ranking in which leftover git-worktree and occupancy files are small relative to the 20-minute gap, or a measured Windows full-suite `--coverage` wall clock under 20 minutes. Neither exists on disk at this ceiling.
